evidence: The binary policy checks 1218 consequences across 669 sites with 635 inconclusive sites. The largest regression, edit 40, spends 0.61726 cumulative profiled seconds transporting/checking supports (including 0.56672 RUP checking), versus 0.28442 compiling seven closures. Nested cumulative times overlap.
limitation: Two alternating repetitions on exposed edits with provisioned origin banks. Native dispatch and gate counters do not bound total work or memory. Greater local closure does not establish a whole-query benefit; comparisons retain every regression.
next_target: Build the tentative matching short-guard graph before transporting and RUP-checking every local consequence. A satisfiable superset graph rejects this closure opportunity; a contradictory graph requires checked supports on both witness paths before native source publication. Remove invalid edges and retry within a budget, or retain ordinary fallback. Compare with the eager gate, ordinary search and guided certificate reuse, including unsupported paths, misses and cold replay. A tentative empty clause needs its own checked local unit certificate.
result: Supported short-guard interactions compile to checked native local closures: 25 with unit guards and 34 with binary guards on different live paths. All eight whole queries remain unresolved.
scope: Keep tentative recognition separate from checked authority. Source-support containment, native unit/split recomposition, automatic origin discovery, wider guards, fresh unlabelled evaluation and uniformly efficient arbitrary-CNF closure remain explicit obligations.
secondary_target: Sharing repeated exact core bodies in the separate hint bank remains open, but does not remove this gate preparation cost.
status: experimental; both live gates regress; no default change
